title: Energy for AI
storyline: Who profits when data centers need more power than the grid can supply: the generators, the equipment makers and the pipelines, and the auctions and rules that cap the windfall.

cast.source: docs/research/energy-ai-encounters.md (Explore 1: the regulated side of who keeps the windfall)
XLU and XLE: the Utilities and Energy funds in src/domain/sector-coverage.ts; both are in the tape table of docs/research/energy-ai-encounters.md

forces.name: Power and the grid
forces.why: PJM's capacity auction prices scarcity (capped at $325 a megawatt-day), and ERCOT, NERC and the Texas PUC set the rules for connecting large loads (docs/research/energy-ai-encounters.md, Explore 2; docs/research/ai-energy-constraint.md).

forces.name: Ratepayer and data-center politics
forces.why: Who pays for the grid data centers need is on ballots and in bills, and it decides how much of the windfall a utility may keep; the midterm ledger's leg 6 tracks it (docs/research/events/midterm-elections-2026-11-03.md).

forces.name: Rates
forces.why: Utilities and pipelines borrow heavily to build, so yields move them (the `rates` kind's own definition in src/domain/market-events-types.ts); the Fed's decisions set them.
